nodes.name: "Manager" in URS §3 and §4.7 ("HR and Managers will have access to reporting screens") means the Line Manager role.
"Admin", "HR", "HR/Admin" and "Admin/HR" in the URS name one role, Admin/HR, which manages entitlements, the annual refresh and the leave type rules.
"Medical Leave with Hospital Certificate" (URS §4.5) and "Sick Leave (with Hospital Certificate)" (URS §4.7) are the same leave type.
The "request type" filter of the leave request views (URS §4.7) means the leave type.
An employee can see their own leave entitlement and remaining balance when submitting and viewing leave requests.
For past-date leave requests, "within the current month" (URS §4.1) means the calendar month of the submission date.
The weekly attendance notification (URS §4.3) is sent by email.
Project Managers and Line Managers are also employees and submit their own leave requests through the same submission function as other employees.

The vendor deliverables in URS §7 (technical proposal, prototype, implementation plan, training plan and documentation, support plan) are project deliverables, not system requirements, and are not recorded as REQs.

A policy-violating leave request follows the normal review path: the chosen Project Manager confirms or denies it first, then the Line Manager approves or rejects it. The Line Manager's approval step is the manual review, and the violation is shown to the Line Manager. No extra review step (e.g. by HR) is added.
The month-end cancellation is done automatically by the system (a scheduled job), without any user action.

A leave request whose period includes any day of a month before the submission month is not accepted as a whole, even if it also includes days of the current month; the employee requests only the current-month days. Leave that starts in the current month and continues into the next month is accepted.

The employee chooses the confirming Project Manager on each leave request, at submission; only the chosen Project Manager confirms or denies that request. With a single assigned project, that project's Project Manager is the only choice.
A half-day leave counts as 0.5 day against the employee's leave entitlement.

Where do the people and organisation data come from: employees (including gender and service start date for seniority), the organisational structure (country, city, office, unit, department), each employee's Line Manager and each project's members and Project Manager? Options: (a) maintained in this system by Admin/HR; (b) imported or synchronised from existing HR / project systems (which ones?); (c) a mix (say which data comes from where).

Who confirms a leave request when the employee belongs to several projects (several Project Managers) or to no project? Options: (a) every Project Manager of the projects the leave dates affect; (b) any one of them; (c) a designated primary Project Manager; (d) with no project, the request goes straight to the Line Manager.

What happens to a leave request that is not confirmed or not approved by the end of the calendar month of its leave start date? Options: (a) it stays pending and can still be acted on; (b) it expires or is cancelled automatically; (c) it is rejected automatically; (d) it is approved automatically; (e) it is escalated (to whom?). And how does the rule apply to leave that spans two months, or to a past-date request submitted on the last day of the month?

How is a policy-violating leave request reviewed? (1) Who performs the "manual review": the normal Project Manager then Line Manager steps with the violation highlighted, or an additional review (e.g. by HR)? (2) Which violations are allowed through (e.g. exceeding the remaining entitlement, a leave type the employee is not eligible for, a missing required document)? (3) If approved, what happens to the excess (negative balance, converted to unpaid leave, other)?

Are leave types, eligibility rules and seniority-based entitlements the same for the whole company, or defined per country (or per office or legal entity), since government regulations differ between the countries the company operates in?
In which unit is leave requested and counted? Options: (a) full days only; (b) full and half days (morning / afternoon); (c) hours.

What does the annual refresh do, and is it the same as the year-start entitlement import? In particular: are unused days carried over (up to what limit, until when) or forfeited, and is the refresh triggered by Admin/HR or run automatically on a fixed date?

Can an employee cancel or withdraw a leave request, or change one that is still pending? If so, until when (before confirmation, before approval, after approval but before the leave starts), and does a change to an approved request go through review again?
When is the employee's remaining entitlement reduced: on submission (reserved), on confirmation, or on final approval? Is it restored when a request is denied, rejected or cancelled?
Who approves the leave of a Line Manager, and who confirms and approves when the employee's Project Manager and Line Manager are the same person?
Can a Project Manager or Line Manager delegate confirmation or approval to someone else while they are absent? If so, who can be a delegate and for how long?

Can anyone submit a leave request on behalf of an employee (e.g. a Project Manager for a team member, or HR)? The URS says "Project Managers submitting for themselves", which may imply they can also submit for others.
How are leave days counted: are weekends and public holidays excluded, which days are working days in each country or office, and who maintains the public holiday calendars?

For the Friday attendance notification: (1) which period does it cover (the past week, the month to date, other)? (2) Does a "valid leave request" mean an approved one only, or also one still pending? (3) Who receives it: the employee only, or also the Project Manager / Line Manager / HR? (4) At what time is it sent, in each office's local time zone?
How should the off-work check treat employees who do not use a card scanner on a given day, e.g. remote work, business trips, client-site work, part-time schedules, or offices without scanners?

How does the card scanner system provide its data: interface (API, database view, file export), frequency (real time, daily), content (every swipe, or first check-in and last check-out per day), employee identifier, and is it one system for all countries and offices?

For the year-start entitlement import: what file format and columns are expected, what happens to rows with errors, can it be repeated during the year (e.g. for new joiners), and can Admin/HR also adjust an individual employee's entitlement manually?

Is the list of suggested leave types in §4.7 the set required at go-live? For each type, please give: paid or unpaid, entitlement (fixed days, seniority bands, or none), eligibility (gender, other) and required documents.
How is the organisation organised below country, city and office: what are a "unit" and a "department", and how do they relate to each other and to offices?

Which leave statistics must the reports show (e.g. days taken by leave type, remaining entitlements, absences without leave), for which periods, with what export (Excel, PDF, none)? Which scope does each role see: Line Managers their own unit or department, HR their country or the whole company? Do Project Managers have reports?

Which events send notification emails (e.g. request submitted, confirmed, denied, approved, rejected, reminder before the month-end deadline), to whom, and what must be configurable (templates, recipients, schedule, on/off per event)? Who configures them?
How do users sign in: through the company's single sign-on / identity provider (which one?) or with accounts managed by this system? What session lifetime (idle timeout) and password rules apply?

What are the measurable performance targets: the peak number of concurrent users, and the response time expected for submitting a request and loading dashboards (e.g. 95% of requests within N seconds) at that load?
What availability and recovery targets apply (e.g. monthly availability %, support hours across time zones, maximum data loss and recovery time after a failure)?
Which languages are required, and at go-live or later? Should dates, times and time zones follow each office's locale?
Which browsers (and versions) and devices must be supported (phones, tablets, desktop)? Is a native mobile app out of scope?

Uploaded documents such as hospital certificates contain personal health data. Which data-protection rules apply (e.g. GDPR or local laws), who may view the documents, how long are they kept, and which file types and sizes are accepted?

The URS gives no MoSCoW priority for most requirements (§4.1 – §4.4 use "can" or no modal verb). Please confirm the priority of each requirement, in particular whether submission, confirmation and approval are must-haves.

The minutes (Q-001) say people and organisation data are imported from existing HR systems. Which HR system or systems provide them, through which interface (API, database view, file export) and how often (real time, daily, on demand)? Please also confirm that project assignments and each project's Project Manager come from these HR systems too, and not from a separate project system.

Who confirms a leave request when the employee is assigned to no project? Options: (a) the confirmation step is skipped and the request goes straight to the Line Manager; (b) the Line Manager both confirms and approves; (c) another role confirms (which one?); (d) the case cannot occur, because every employee is always assigned to at least one project.

The minutes say exceeding the remaining entitlement is allowed and is reviewed by the Line Manager. What happens with the other policy violations: (1) a leave type the employee is not eligible for (gender, seniority); (2) a missing required supporting document? For each: (a) also allowed and reviewed by the Line Manager, or (b) blocked at submission?

When a request that exceeds the remaining entitlement is approved, the balance stays at 0. Are the excess days recorded anywhere (for example shown as over-entitlement or unpaid days in the reports, or passed on for payroll), or are they simply not counted?

Requests not confirmed and approved by the end of the leave start month are cancelled. When exactly is the cut-off: the end of the last day of the month in each office's local time zone, or in one company time zone? Is there any grace period, for example for a past-date request submitted on the last day of the month, which would otherwise be cancelled the same day unless both the Project Manager and the Line Manager act on it?

Leave can be taken in half days (morning / afternoon). How does the weekly attendance check (a day is off work with no check-in or with less than 4 hours of presence) treat a day with a half-day leave? For example, if an employee has a half-day leave and less than 4 hours of presence, is the day reported as off work with a valid leave request, as off work without a leave request, or not reported at all?
